input_oneliner: New admit: 71M prior MI and HTN, 5 days worsening bilateral leg swelling, sleeping in recliner, weight up 4 kg, SpO2 93% RA

optional_context.objective: weight +4 kg, SpO2 93% on room air

reference_targets_freetext.item: Jugular venous pressure with abdominojugular reflux
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Elevated JVP and positive abdominojugular reflux are the strongest bedside findings for elevated filling pressures

reference_targets_freetext.item: Auscultate for a third heart sound (S3) at the apex in left lateral decubitus
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: S3 has a high positive likelihood ratio for decompensated heart failure

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (number of pillows, waking breathless)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Orthopnea/PND point to left-sided congestion rather than peripheral or drug edema

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about recently started or up-titrated amlodipine or other dihydropyridine, NSAIDs, thiazolidinediones, gabapentinoids
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Drug-induced edema mimics HF and resolves with withdrawal

reference_targets_freetext.item: Lung bases for crackles and dullness (effusion); pitting depth and whether edema extends to sacrum
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Extent of congestion and dependent distribution support HF over venous insufficiency

should_not_recommend: Large IV fluid bolus before JVP and lung examination
Empiric compression stockings or leg elevation as the plan without assessing filling pressures
Ordering an echocardiogram as a substitute for JVP and cardiac auscultation
